reason: *n̥mr̥tó- + *h₂éwsōs, both exact in Gk and II (builder agrees). Bacchyl. 17.42 ἀμβρότου … Ἀοῦς (GLAUx 0199-002: ἀμβρότου fem. gen. ATR of Ἀοῦς, in ἐραννὸν Ἀοῦς φάος; GLAUx lemma Ἀών is wrong), RV 1.113.13 (VNH: 13a puróṣā́ḥ = purā́ uṣā́ḥ … devī́, 13d ajárāmŕ̥tā, nom. fem. sg. predicated of Dawn). West ch. 5 names the pair. The scan's RV 7.75.3b misconstrual is correctly dropped. Caveats: Greek has it once, in 5th-c. lyric, not Homer, and ἄμβροτος is a broad divine epithet. The Vedic is predicative in another pāda, the Greek attributive. Oxytone n̥mr̥téh₂ against Ved. amŕ̥tā (root-accented in the privative compound; the r5 open point for bp-ii-ita-003) is the handbook form; a caveat, not a contradicted type.

*wiHrós + *h₁éḱwos, both exact in Ce and II. Síaburcharpat Con Culainn (CELT G301008; = LU G301900) bátar anála fer ⁊ ech, gen. pl., men first; RV 9.96.11d vīrébhir áśvair (VNH, a true two-member pair, men first); AVŚ 12.1.25 aśveṣu vīreṣu (DCS ctr 25, inside a list); Yt. 15 = CAB YtWay12.12a aspaēšu vīraēšu (heads a vīspaēšu list). The generic objection is met: West ch. 12 (with Benveniste, Wackernagel, Schmitt 1967) treats horses-and-men as inherited, and the shared lexical choice is *wiHrós, not *h₂nḗr, in Celtic, Italic (uiris equisque) and Indo-Iranian (also YtMihr26.4f/h aspaēca paiti vīraēca … aspa.vīraja). Caveats: the Irish is one prose instance in an LU text with a Patrician frame; -kʷe is interpolated (OIr ⁊, Vedic asyndeton). Italic (Cic. Off. 3.116 uiris equisque 'ut dicitur') would make it three branches if checked locally.

*ish₁rós *ménos, both exact in Gk and II, the same formations and accent. Od. 7.167, Od. 8.2 ἱερὸν μένος Ἀλκινόοιο (AGDT: nom. SBJ, ATR), Hymn. Hom. 3.371 ἱερὸν μένος Ἠελίοιο (GLAUx 0013-003), RV 8.48.7a iṣiréṇa te mánasā (VNH). Schulze's equation, endorsed by West ch. 2. Caveats: there is one Vedic instance, in the instrumental against the Greek nominative periphrasis, and Greek μένος here is 'might', not 'mind'.

*h₁éḱwos + *h₂nḗr, both exact in Gk and II, but overclaimed. The Greek is a real stock coordination (Il. 23.242 ἵπποι τε καὶ ἄνδρες, Il. 10.338 ἵππων τε καὶ ἀνδρῶν; AGDT). The only Vedic parallel, RV 10.68.12cd (VNH), is a four-member anaphoric list (sá góbhiḥ sá áśvaiḥ sá vīrébhiḥ sá nŕ̥bhir) with vīrébhiḥ between horses and men, so it is not the pair. The inherited 'men' word of the formula is *wiHrós (epic-diction-006); Greek ἀνήρ is the renewal, so the Gk+II *h₂nḗr pairing is probably independent in each branch (generic pair). Nominative and -kʷe are interpolated.

Reject edge. *deywós is exact in II and It. The head *ǵénh₁os is exact in Latin only; Ved. jánman- (RV 6.51.2b, 1.70.6b devā́nāṃ jánma, VNH) is another formation (root level). Both Latin witnesses are on round 4's derivative list (rule 3): Catull. 64.23 heroes, salvete, deum genus (Perseus, l. 23; it renders the Hesiodic 'divine race of heroes') and Lucr. 5.1156 divom genus humanumque (Perseus, l. 1156). So the only branch with the head in the line's formation is a probable calque. West ch. 3 equates Ved. jánas- with γένος, but neither is cited here, and Greek renewed *deywós.

*h₁wésus *ménos, both exact in Gk and Ir (builder agrees), but the passages are not parallel. Il. 17.456, 24.442 μένος ἠΰ (AGDT: acc. object of 'breathed into' horses) means 'good courage'. Y. 34.8c vohū … manō and Y. 48.12b vohū manaŋhā (CAB) are Gathic 'Good Thought', a theological term and the name of an Aməša Spənta. West ch. 2 compares μένος ἠΰ with the non-cognate Ved. bhadrám mánaḥ, not with vohu manah, so the drafter's pairing has no cited scholarly claim (the compounds εὐμενής ~ humanah- are the real inherited equation). There is no Vedic vásu- + mánas-.

*ménos is exact in Gk and II, but the NP head is noun plus modifier (r2 rule), and the modifier is root level in both. Gk μένος πολυθαρσές (Il. 17.156, 19.37; AGDT) has the s-stem compound adjective; Ved. dhr̥ṣán mánaḥ (RV 1.54.3b, 5.35.4c; VNH) has dhr̥ṣát. The engine's nasal-present participle dʰr̥snuwónt is the formation of neither; the builder's II 'exact' for dhr̥ṣ- reaches the nasal present through the root (the builder still gives level none overall). West ch. 2 names the pair (as RV 1.54.2, a numbering slip).

The wording is a commonplace with no scholarly claim of inherited phrasing. West ch. 8 compares AVŚ 4.12.6 práti tiṣṭhordhváḥ (DCS: the closing prose imperative to the cured patient) with Pind. The head verb is root level in both, with different stems and valency, and the engine's intransitive root-aorist imperative sth₂dʰí is in neither. Only ὀρθός = ūrdhvá- is shared at formation level (builder mapping gap for AV ūrdhva). The drafter declined the identical posture collocation (Il. 23.271 ~ RV 1.164.10b) as generic, and the healing context does not change the wording.

The only exact item is the noun *kʷoynéh₂ = kaēnā- (a sound equation), which is periphery here, as an instrumental the line invents.
